slides.title: Welcome to DOM Manipulation
slides.content:
# DOM Manipulation 🌐

The **DOM** (**Document Object Model**) is the programming interface for HTML. When a web browser loads a page, it constructs an in-memory tree of objects representing every HTML tag.

## What you'll master:
- 🌳 **The DOM Tree** - Nodes, elements, parents, and children
- 🎯 **Selecting Elements** - `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll`, and `getElementById`
- ✏️ **Modifying Content** - `textContent`, `innerHTML`, and security considerations
- 🎨 **Modifying Styles & Classes** - `style` object and `classList` API
- 🏗️ **Creating & Removing Nodes** - `createElement`, `append`, and `remove`

slides.title: The DOM Tree Representation
slides.content: # The DOM Tree Representation 🌳 The browser turns HTML markup into a tree structure of JavaScript objects: ``` document │ ┌───────┴───────┐ │ │ ┌────┴────┐ <header> <main> │ │ <h1> <p> ``` Through JavaScript, every single node in this tree can be queried, styled, moved, animated, or deleted!

slides.title: Modifying Content: textContent vs innerHTML
slides.content:
# Modifying Content: `textContent` vs `innerHTML` ✏️ ## 1. `textContent` (Safe & Fast): Sets or retrieves pure plain text without parsing HTML tags: ```javascript_not const title = document.querySelector('h1'); title.textContent = "Welcome to Our Platform!"; ``` ## 2. `innerHTML` (Parses HTML tags): Parses the string as real HTML markup: ```javascript_not const container = document.querySelector('#feed'); container.innerHTML = "

User Alice posted an update.

"; ``` > 🚨 **Critical Security Alert:** Never pass un-sanitized user input into `innerHTML`! Doing so creates Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities where hackers can inject malicious `

slides.title: Modifying Attributes
Custom Data Attributes (dataset)
slides.content:
# Custom Data Attributes (`dataset`) 🏷️

HTML5 `data-*` attributes are accessible through the `.dataset` property in JavaScript:

```html_not
<button id="buy-btn" data-product-id="1054" data-price="49.99">Buy Now</button>
```

```javascript_not
const btn = document.getElementById('buy-btn');

// Read data attributes (converted automatically to camelCase!)
console.log(btn.dataset.productId); // "1054"
console.log(btn.dataset.price);     // "49.99"

// Write/update data attributes
btn.dataset.inStock = "true"; // Adds data-in-stock="true"
```

DOM Performance Best Practices
slides.content:
# DOM Performance Checklist 🏎️

1. **Batch DOM Updates:** Use `DocumentFragment` when creating lists of elements.
2. **Prefer `classList` over inline styles:** Keeps CSS and JS separated cleanly.
3. **Use `textContent` over `innerHTML`:** Immune to XSS vulnerabilities.
4. **Cache Selectors:** Don't run `document.querySelector('.card')` 100 times in a loop; store it in a `const`!

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# DOM Manipulation Mastered! 🌟

You can now dynamically query, style, generate, and animate any webpage element!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Selecting:** Use `querySelector` (single) and `querySelectorAll` (multiple).
- ✅ **Content:** Use `textContent` for safety; avoid un-sanitized `innerHTML`.
- ✅ **Attributes:** Use `getAttribute`, `setAttribute`, and `dataset` for `data-*`.
- ✅ **Classes:** Manipulate styling with `classList.add()`, `.remove()`, and `.toggle()`.
- ✅ **Performance:** Batch insertions with `DocumentFragment`.
